paper.title_en: Dynamical instability of expansion-free cylindrical spacetime in matter-geometry coupled gravity theory
paper.abstract_en: This study examines the dynamical instability in cylindrical fluid configuration undergoing non-expanding evolution within the framework of a matter-geometry coupled gravitational theory. A perturbation scheme is initially employed to derive the dynamical equations governing the system's evolution and to analyze the stability across the Newtonian, post-Newtonian, and post-post-Newtonian regimes. These results indicate that the adiabatic index fails to play any role for stability within the standard Newtonian or post-Newtonian approximations. Our results indicate that the instability region is instead dictated by alternative parameters, which exhibit strong agreement with earlier investigations into self-gravitating collapse. We also use junction conditions to smoothly match the interior spacetime with a suitable exterior line element. We conclude that the dynamics of the cylindrical fluid configuration under consideration are primarily dictated by key physical quantities, namely, the energy density and the principal (radial, tangential, and axial) stresses.
